boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Ware Bottom Church record (May 20, 1864) in the Bermuda Hundred Campaign [May 1864]. The Proctor's Creek record (VA053) ends on May 16. The frozen description's reinforcement of Lee's army from Beauregard's force is campaign contribution, not this record's result. Army-wide returns, the campaign-wide casualty return and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads 'Divisions (10,000 total)' and the frozen and live descriptions say about 10,000 troops were involved; the live force field reads zero. Humphreys says that after the detachments Butler retained about 10,000 enlisted infantry, Kautz's 2,600 cavalry and about 2,000 colored cavalry, that Smith took very nearly 16,000 infantry, and that Beauregard kept about 9,000 infantry.
claims.rationale: The 10,000 is an undivided summary figure; Humphreys' figures describe the forces after the detachments to the Army of the Potomac of late May, not May 20. None is adopted as a matched opening strength; live zeros are not measured absence.

open_questions: Ames's, Terry's, Howell's and the regimental reports of May 20, Walker's, Wise's and Martin's casualty reports (Nos. 103, 106), Beauregard's June 2 telegram and the May 5-31 Union casualty return (garbled) remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live NPS page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Humphreys' The Virginia Campaign of ’64 and ’65 (1883) is an interested history by the Army of the Potomac's chief of staff, in the same author family as the registered From Gettysburg to the Rapidan; for this campaign it summarizes Smith's, Gillmore's and Weitzel's reports and quotes Beauregard's reports and telegrams, so it is not independent of the Beauregard family. Butler's telegrams and Hagood's, Barton's and Beauregard's reports, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XXXVI, Part 2, are separate families of interested commanders' accounts; the volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
